claims.text: `evict_oldest(&mut self, n: usize)` looped `for _ in 0..=n`, so it popped up to n+1 entries off `order` and removed them from `map` rather than n.

The method returned nothing, so callers had no way to learn how many entries were actually removed; when `order` was already empty the `if let Some(..)` arm simply did nothing and the loop kept spinning for the remaining iterations.

citations.item: pub fn kvstore::cache::Cache::evict(&mut self, usize) -> usize

claims.text: `evict(&mut self, n: usize) -> usize` loops `0..n`, `break`s on the `None` arm when `order` runs dry, and returns the `removed` counter — so it removes at most n entries and reports the count.
Its doc comment now states the return value: "Evict the `n` oldest entries, returning how many were removed."
A new `capacity(&self) -> usize` returns `max_entries`, documented as "The configured maximum number of entries."
`put` is otherwise unchanged: it still computes `overflow = self.map.len() - self.max_entries` and asks for `overflow + 1`, only now via `evict`, and discards the returned count.
`kvstore/src/cache.rs` no longer contains `evict_oldest`; it now contains `evict` and `capacity` instead.

The `put` → `evict_oldest` call edge is gone and a `put` → `evict` call edge takes its place; the structural diff treats this as a likely rename (confidence 0.75, same file and overlapping source range).

claims.text: The public API delta for the `kvstore` package is two additions and one removal, and cargo-public-api assigns `requiredBump: major` under the `inherent_method_missing` lint ("pub method removed or renamed", at `Cache::evict_oldest`, kvstore/src/cache.rs:41).
`handle_request` in kvstore/src/api.rs reaches the changed code one hop away through a `calls` edge to `Cache::put`, and could be affected — the impact set reports possibilities, not certainties.
Any out-of-tree caller of `evict_oldest` no longer compiles, since that method is removed from the public API rather than deprecated.

`put`'s eviction behaviour changed silently: it still requests `overflow + 1`, but the callee no longer removes an extra entry, so each `put` that trips the bound now evicts one fewer entry than before. Whether the cache still stays at or below `max_entries` depends on that `+ 1` still being the right argument.
The one caller in this file discards the new return value, so the count `evict` reports is currently unused inside the crate.
`capacity` and the pre-existing `free_slots` now sit side by side and both derive from `max_entries`; check that the two accessors are meant to coexist.

`evict` removes keys from `map` only for entries present in `order`, and `put` pushes every key onto `order` including repeats, so the relationship between `order` length and `map` length is worth confirming against the new bounded loop.
The release needs a major version bump; the structural diff records no package version changes in this commit.

output.summary: In `kvstore/src/cache.rs`, the public method `Cache::evict_oldest(&mut self, usize)` is replaced by `Cache::evict(&mut self, usize) -> usize`, which stops when the queue is empty and returns how many entries it actually removed; the old loop ran `0..=n`, removing one more entry than asked for. A new accessor `Cache::capacity(&self) -> usize` returning `max_entries` is added, and `Cache::put` is updated to call `evict` instead of `evict_oldest`. cargo-public-api records this as a major bump: `pub method removed or renamed`.
